label: 6061-T6 Aluminum
guidance: The general-purpose default: strong, light, corrosion-resistant, and easy to machine. A good choice when you are not sure which aluminum you need.

label: 7075-T6 Aluminum
guidance: Higher strength than 6061, closer to steel, at a higher material cost. Common for aerospace and high-load parts.

label: 2024-T3 Aluminum
guidance: High strength and fatigue resistance, widely used in aerospace structures. Less corrosion-resistant than 6061, so it is often coated.

label: 5052-H32 Aluminum
guidance: Excellent corrosion resistance and formability. A common pick for sheet-metal parts, enclosures, and marine use.

label: 6063-T6 Aluminum
guidance: Smooth surface finish and good corrosion resistance. Often used for extrusions, frames, and architectural parts.

label: 1018 Steel
guidance: Low-cost, easy-to-machine mild steel. Good for fixtures, shafts, and general-purpose parts that will be painted or plated.

label: 1045 Steel
guidance: Medium-carbon steel with more strength and wear resistance than 1018. Used for gears, axles, and bolts.

label: 4140 Steel
guidance: Strong, tough alloy steel that can be heat-treated. Common for shafts, tooling, and high-stress components.

label: A36 Steel
guidance: Inexpensive structural steel for brackets, plates, and welded assemblies. Surface finish is rougher than cold-rolled grades.

label: 303 Stainless Steel
guidance: The easiest stainless to machine. Good corrosion resistance for fittings, fasteners, and general turned parts.

label: 304 Stainless Steel
guidance: The most common stainless: corrosion-resistant and food-safe. Used for enclosures, brackets, and food or medical-adjacent parts.

label: 316 Stainless Steel
guidance: Better corrosion resistance than 304, especially against salt water and chemicals. Common for marine and medical parts.

label: 17-4 PH Stainless Steel
guidance: Very strong, heat-treatable stainless. Used where stainless corrosion resistance and steel-like strength are both needed.

label: Grade 2 Titanium
guidance: Light, extremely corrosion-resistant, and biocompatible. Common for medical, marine, and chemical-processing parts.

label: Grade 5 Titanium (Ti-6Al-4V)
guidance: The strongest common titanium alloy, with an excellent strength-to-weight ratio. Standard for aerospace and high-performance parts.

label: C360 Brass
guidance: Extremely easy to machine with a clean finish. Used for fittings, valves, connectors, and decorative hardware.

label: C110 Copper
guidance: Excellent electrical and thermal conductivity. Used for bus bars, terminals, heat sinks, and RF parts.

label: ABS
guidance: Low-cost, tough, and easy to machine. A good general-purpose plastic for prototypes, housings, and covers.

label: Acetal Homopolymer (Delrin)
guidance: Low friction, stiff, and dimensionally stable. The usual pick for gears, bushings, and sliding parts.

label: Acetal Copolymer
guidance: Similar to Delrin with better chemical and hot-water resistance. Good for gears, bushings, and fluid-handling parts.

label: Polycarbonate
guidance: Very impact-resistant and available clear. Used for guards, windows, covers, and parts that take abuse.

label: Nylon 6/6
guidance: Strong, wear-resistant, and self-lubricating. Common for bushings, rollers, and structural plastic parts. Absorbs moisture over time.

label: Nylon 6
guidance: Tough cast nylon for larger wear parts such as sheaves, wear pads, and rollers.

label: Glass-Filled Nylon (30%)
guidance: Much stiffer and more dimensionally stable than unfilled nylon. Used for structural brackets and housings.

label: Cast Acrylic (PMMA)
guidance: Crystal-clear and polishable. Used for windows, displays, light pipes, and covers. More brittle than polycarbonate.

label: HDPE
guidance: Low-cost, chemical-resistant, and easy to cut. Used for tanks, trays, cutting surfaces, and outdoor parts.

label: UHMW-PE
guidance: Extremely wear-resistant with a very slippery surface. Used for guides, rails, liners, and conveyor parts.

label: PEEK
guidance: Premium plastic for high heat, chemicals, and strength. Common in medical, aerospace, and semiconductor parts. Material cost is high.

label: PEI (Ultem)
guidance: Strong, flame-resistant, and stable at high temperature. Used for electrical, medical, and aerospace components.

label: PTFE (Teflon)
guidance: The lowest-friction plastic, with outstanding chemical and heat resistance. Soft, so tolerances are harder to hold. Used for seals and insulators.

label: PVC
guidance: Low-cost, chemical-resistant, and easy to bond. Used for fluid handling, electrical insulation, and general-purpose panels.
